source.title: Not All Features Are Created Equal: A Mechanistic Study of Vision-Language-Action Models
source.authors: Bryce Grant; Xijia Zhao; Peng Wang

page_placements.theme: What units match, and how interpretable they are, varies with layer depth

record.tranche_reason: The paper analyzes neuron-to-concept associations in VLA pathways, but does not measure the share of neurons with one main job or test explanations on held-out activating examples. Its findings therefore do not test any listed claim version.
record.gate_note: The paper reports neuron-category associations and counts, but does not establish that individual neurons have one exclusive, human-nameable job or quantify how many do. These results are recorded as related findings under versions ["none"]. The paper’s results on SAE feature ablation and pooling are not neuron job-prevalence tests.
record.test_reason: This is a VLA interpretability study of activation injection, counterfactual prompts, SAE pooling and probes. It never measures what share of neurons have one main job, and it never scores neuron explanations against held-out activations or simulated activations. Its introduction assumes the premise the claim disputes: SAEs extract "sparse monosemantic features from the polysemantic activations". It neither tests nor cites the claim's sources. The only neuron-level result is App. F.2, which projects FFN weight vectors onto a token vocabulary and counts neurons per concept category. That is a category-association count, not a per-neuron job audit or a validated explanation.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase covers only App. F.2 and misses the paper's main conclusions. Across six architectures, fine-tuned VLAs learn coordinate-bound motor programs: cross-task expert injection makes π0.5 follow the source trajectory in 99.6% of episodes. The programs are selected by vision and executed by the expert pathway. Language matters mainly when the scene is ambiguous. The goal sits in the VLM pathway and can be restored by one edit on 4 of 5 architectures. SAE pooling should be chosen per architecture, and temporal-contrastive SAEs hurt every architecture tested. The authors draw no conclusion about how many neurons have one main job.
record.recipe_differences: Uses token-vocabulary projections of FFN weight vectors and fine-grained neuron concept mapping in VLA pathways, rather than auditing neuron poles with explanations tested on held-out activations.
record.method_sensitivity: Neuron-category counts and associations vary by layer; the paper also reports different mapping patterns for π0.5 and OpenVLA-OFT.

fits_no_version.finding: In App. F.2, FFN weight projection onto a token vocabulary assigns large fractions of π0.5 PaliGemma neurons to coarse motor and scene categories. Motion verbs rise from 25.8% at L0 to 40.3% at L17. OpenVLA-OFT shows spatial-concept neuron counts growing across layers.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In VLA backbones, FFN neurons' vocabulary-projection associations shift across depth from object and spatial concepts toward motion and gripper concepts. This is not evidence on neurons having a single validated job.

record.problems: The neuron-category associations are not tested as exclusive neuron jobs, and the paper does not report held-out validation of neuron explanations. The described neuron mappings are category-level and are not accompanied by uncertainty estimates.
record.rows_left_out: No other neuron-category counts were omitted. SAE feature ablation and pooling results were not included because they measure SAE features or rollout fidelity, not neuron job prevalence.

untested.parts: No audit of Qwen3-32B neuron poles and no job-share estimate.
No per-neuron job shares in any model. The VLAs studied (80M–7B) are not audited for interpretable-neuron share.
No analysis of InceptionV1 or of canonical polysemantic neurons.
No comparison of interpretable-neuron share across architectures or tools.
No neuron-based attribution graphs. Circuit-level work uses SAEs and residual-stream injection.
No test of whether neuron explanations predict firing.
No simulation-based scoring of neuron explanations.

record.verdict_notes: Relation changed from 'discusses' to 'assumes'. The paper never discusses the claim, but its framing presumes polysemantic activations that need SAEs. Tranche T6 is kept. App. B notes that some SAE features lack a clean semantic reading. That concerns SAE features, not neurons, so it is not evidence for V6 or V7. The App. F.2 counts are weight-vocabulary projections, not activation-based. The paper gives no association threshold, and the categories may overlap.

versions.untested_parts: No audit of Qwen3-32B neuron poles or estimate of the share with one or two jobs or not-yet-understood poles.
No cross-model estimate of neuron-pole job shares, no dense-versus-MoE comparison, and no trillion-parameter models.
No analysis of InceptionV1’s cat-and-car neuron or recursive generalization.
No comparison of interpretable-neuron shares across architectures, regularization choices, or explanation tools; no InceptionV1-sized vision-model estimates.
No attribution graphs built from model neurons and no comparison with replacement-model reconstruction error.
No test of explanations against new activating examples or prediction of where a neuron fires.
No automated scoring of neuron explanations by simulated activations on new text.

relation.reason: The intro takes it as given that SAEs pull monosemantic features out of polysemantic LM activations (line 64). App. F.2 treats FFN neurons as concept units without testing that. The paper never discusses the neurons-already-clean claim, so 'discusses' doesn't fit and 'assumes' does.

tranche.reason: This VLA mechanistic study counts how FFN weight projections associate with vocabulary categories. It never measures what share of neurons have one main job and never scores explanations against activations, so it neither tests nor uses the claim.

source_check.notes: Both rows match App. F.2. The counts come from projecting weights onto a token vocabulary in a VLA (π0.5's PaliGemma 3B backbone), with no exclusivity or activation-based validation, so they bear on no version. No verdicts are listed.

statements.problem: None. The 25.8% at L0 and 40.3% at L17 figures match App. F.2 for PaliGemma FFN weight projection. 'Assigned' paraphrases the text's 'associate with', which is fine.
